---
title: "Getting Started"
description: "Quick guide to using eoread for reading satellite products as xarray Datasets"
---

## Installation

Install eoread from the HYGEOS package index:

```bash
hyp add --hygeos eoread
```

## Core Concept

Every eoread reader function returns a lazy `xarray.Dataset` backed by dask arrays. Data is only loaded from disk when you explicitly compute or access a variable. This enables efficient out-of-core processing of large satellite products.

```python
from eoread.msi import Level1_MSI

# Returns a lazy xarray.Dataset — nothing is read from disk yet
ds = Level1_MSI("S2A_MSIL1C_20231028T094350_N0509_R071_T30TUH_20231028T130711.SAFE")
print(ds)
```

## Reading Products

### Sensor-Specific Readers

Each supported sensor has a dedicated reader function. The naming convention is `Level{level}_{sensor}`:

```python
from eoread.msi import Level1_MSI
from eoread.olci import Level1_OLCI, Level2_OLCI
from eoread.meris import Level1_MERIS
from eoread.oli import Level1_OLI
from eoread.modis import Level1_MODIS
from eoread.ecostress import Level1C_ECOSTRESS
from eoread.pace import Level1B_PACE_OCI
from eoread.venus import Level1_VENUS
from eoread.sgli import Level1_SGLI
from eoread.hypso import Level1_HYPSO
from eoread.goesng import Level1_GOESNG
```

### Auto-Detection

The `Level1()` and `Level2()` functions automatically detect the sensor type from the filename and dispatch to the appropriate reader:

```python
from eoread.autodetect import Level1, Level2
from pathlib import Path

# Automatically detects Sentinel-2 MSI from the filename
ds = Level1(Path("S2A_MSIL1C_20231028T094350_N0509_R071_T30TUH_20231028T130711.SAFE"))

# Automatically detects Sentinel-3 OLCI Level-2
ds_l2 = Level2(Path("S3A_OL_2_WFR____20231028T094655_00900146_20231028T095035_00100285_0030_0025_0010.SEN3"))
```

## Dataset Variables

All readers produce a consistent set of standard variables:

| Variable | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `Lttoa` | Top-of-atmosphere radiance |
| `Rtoa` | Top-of-atmosphere reflectance |
| `lat`, `lon` | Latitude/longitude rasters |
| `sza`, `saa` | Solar zenith and azimuth angles |
| `vza`, `vaa` | View zenith and azimuth angles |
| `central_wavelength` | Central wavelength per band |

### Example: Inspecting a Dataset

```python
from eoread.msi import Level1_MSI

ds = Level1_MSI("S2A_MSIL1C_20231028T094350_N0509_R071_T30TUH_20231028T130711.SAFE",
                chunks=1000, resolution=60)

print(ds.data_vars)
print(ds.coords)
print(ds.attrs["metadata"])
```

## Chunking

All readers accept a `chunks` parameter to control the spatial block size for dask:

```python
# Square chunks of 500 pixels (default for most readers)
ds = Level1_MSI("product.SAFE", chunks=500)

# Different chunk sizes for rows and columns
ds = Level1_MSI("product.SAFE", chunks=(1000, 500))
```

> **Tip:** Align chunks with your processing pipeline. For best performance, set chunking as late as possible — after any subsetting operations.

## Subsetting

Since eoread returns standard `xarray.Dataset` objects, you can use all of xarray's subsetting capabilities:

```python
# Subset by row/column indices
sub = ds.isel(rows=slice(500, 1500), columns=slice(400, 1400))

# Subset by coordinate values
sub = ds.sel(lat=slice(45.5, 46.0), lon=slice(3.0, 3.5))
```

You can also use helper functions from the `core` package for geographic subsetting:

```python
from core.tools import sub_rect, sub_pt

# Subset by bounding box (lat/lon in degrees)
sub = sub_rect(ds, lat_min=45.0, lon_min=3.0, lat_max=46.0, lon_max=4.0)

# Subset by center point and radius (radius in km)
sub = sub_pt(ds, pt_lat=45.5, pt_lon=3.5, rad=10)
```

## Resolution Resampling

Some readers support resampling all bands to a common resolution:

```python
# Sentinel-2: resample all bands to 10m
ds = Level1_MSI("product.SAFE", resolution=10)

# MODIS: resample all bands to 250m
ds = Level1_MODIS("MOD021KM.A2023001.0000.hdf", resolution=250)
```

When `resolution=None`, bands keep their native resolutions and are stored as separate variables.

## Quality Flags

The `GenericFlags` enumeration provides a sensor-agnostic interface to quality flags:

```python
from eoread.flags import GenericFlags

# Access cloud flag
cloud_mask = ds.attrs["flags"].getflag(ds, GenericFlags.CLOUD)

# Access land mask
land_mask = ds.attrs["flags"].getflag(ds, GenericFlags.LAND)

# Access L1 invalid pixels
invalid_mask = ds.attrs["flags"].getflag(ds, GenericFlags.L1_INVALID)
```

Available flags:

| Flag | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `LAND` | Land/water mask |
| `CLOUD` | Cloud detection |
| `L1_INVALID` | Invalid L1 pixels |
| `L1_DEGRADED` | Degraded quality pixels |

## Computing Results

Data is loaded lazily. To trigger computation:

```python
# Compute a single variable
rtoa_values = ds.Rtoa.compute()

# Compute the entire dataset
ds_computed = ds.compute()

# Write to NetCDF (triggers computation automatically)
ds.to_netcdf("output.nc")
```

## Metadata Filtering

By default, readers include all metadata in the dataset attributes. To reduce memory usage, you can filter metadata:

```python
# No metadata
ds = Level1_MSI("product.SAFE", metadata_template=[])

# Only specific metadata keys
ds = Level1_MSI("product.SAFE", metadata_template=[
    ["General_Info", "Product_Info", "PROCESSING_BASELINE"],
    ["Product_Identifier"]
])
```

## Version Compatibility

Some readers support a `v1_compat=True` flag to produce output compatible with eoread v1:

```python
ds = Level1_OLCI("product.SEN3", v1_compat=True)
```
